nodes.procedure: The Ni foam was immersed in 3.0 M HCl under ultrasonic treatment for 10 min and then repeatedly cleaned using ethanol and deionized water. Subsequently, it was dried for 5 h at 60 °C in a vacuum oven.

nodes.name: FRCD electro-oxidation
nodes.procedure: NiOOH supported on Ni foam was prepared using an improved Fast-Repeated-Charging/Discharging (FRCD) electro-oxidation process. In a typical experiment, the anode was prepared using a 1×2.5 cm² Ni foam, and the cathode contained an approximately 1×1 cm² platinum sheet. The anode and cathode were then immersed in 45 mL of 2.0 M KOH. The cathode and anode were repeatedly charged and discharged at a current of 400 mA (~2.8 V) for 4 hours using a CT3001A battery testing system. Finally, the laminar NiOOH was synthesized in situ on the Ni foam.

nodes.name: Sulfur doping
nodes.procedure: First, the NiOOH was immersed in 30 mL of 27 mM sodium sulfide aqueous solution. The mixture was then transferred into a water bath kettle and heated at 80 °C for 1 h to obtain NiOOH@Ni3S2.

nodes.name: Cobalt ion exchange hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: Typically, the as-obtained NiOOH@Ni3S2 was added to 35 mL of 13 mM cobalt nitrate aqueous solution. After 15 min of stirring, the mixture was transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 150 °C for 7 h. The NiCo-LDH@CoNi2S4 was obtained through washing with deionized water several times and dried at 60 °C for 12 h in a vacuum oven.

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained NiCo-LDH@CoNi2S4 and NaH2PO2·H2O were placed at two separate positions in a porcelain boat with 1.5 g NaH2PO2·H2O at the upstream side of the furnace. The porcelain boat was placed at the center of a tube furnace at 300 °C for 1 h under an argon gas flow. After being allowed to cool to room temperature naturally, the Ni–Co–P@CoNi2S4 was obtained, washed with deionized water and then dried at 60 °C for 12 h in a vacuum oven.

nodes.name: Electrochemical reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The Ni–Co–P@CoNi2S4 was further electrochemical reconstructed in 2.0 M KOH aqueous electrolyte with cyclic voltammetry (CV) test between -0.2 and 0.6 V (at a scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹) in three-electrode system. After 20 cycles, the Ni–Co oxyhydroxides were synthesized via P and S leaching-induced strategy, and the Ni–Co oxyhydroxides were obtained through washed with deionized water and ethanol, then dried at 40 °C for 12 h in a vacuum oven (high mass loading of 6 mg cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni–Co oxyhydroxides display 3D vertically standing and cross-linked nanoplate arrays consisting of 2D hexagonal nanosheets with nanoplates of 6-8 μm lateral size and 400-600 nm thickness, and attached hexagonal nanosheets of 200-300 nm lateral size and 20-30 nm thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of the Ni–Co oxyhydroxides display three-dimensional (3D) vertically standing and cross-linked nanoplate arrays consisting of two-dimensional (2D) hexagonal nanosheets, whose formation is mainly due to the electrochemical reconstruction (Fig. 1a and S7†). The nanoplates have a lateral size of 6-8 μm and a thickness of 400·600 nm m, and the attached hexagonal nanosheets show a lateral size of 200-300 nm and a thickness of 20-30 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals crystalline–amorphous interfaces with interplanar spacings of 0.236 nm and 0.209 nm for γ-NiOOH (102) and (105) planes, 0.242 nm and 0.220 nm for γ-CoOOH (101) and (006) planes, and 0.249 nm for NiOOH (110) plane; abundant defects indicate ionic vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A large number of crystalline and amorphous regions are scattered over the nanoplate, as confirmed by the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image... the interplanar spacing was determined to be 0.236 and 0.209 nm, corresponding to the (102) and (105) planes of γ-NiOOH, and the lattice spacing of 0.242 and 0.220 nm corresponded to the (101) and (006) crystal planes of γ-CoOOH... the lattice spacing of 0.249 nm corresponds to the (110) plane of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD demonstrates typical mixed phase consisting of γ-NiOOH, γ-CoOOH and NiOOH phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern demonstrates that the as-formed Ni–Co oxyhydroxides show a typical mixed phase consisting of γ-NiOOH, γ-CoOOH and NiOOH phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectrum fitted to Ni³⁺ (855.4/873.1 eV) and Ni⁴⁺ (857.4/875.8 eV) with average Ni valence 3.3 consistent with γ-NiOOH; Co 2p shows Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺ (780.3/795.6 eV and 783.7/798.5 eV) with average Co valence 3.27 associated with γ-CoOOH; increased Ni³⁺/Ni⁴⁺ and Co oxidation state indicate cationic vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectrum for the Ni–Co oxyhydroxides was fitted to two spin–orbit peaks (2p₃/₂ and 2p₁/₂, around 855.4/873.1 for Ni³⁺ and 857.4/875.8 eV for Ni⁴⁺, resulting in an average Ni valence of 3.3, in line with γ-NiOOH... The peaks at 780.3/795.6 eV and 783.7/798.5 eV correspond to Co³⁺/Co⁴⁺ in the high-resolution Co 2p spectrum of the Ni–Co oxyhydroxides, revealing an average cobalt valence of 3.27, which is associated with γ-CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during electrochemical reconstruction shows formation of γ-NiOOH peaks at 465 cm⁻¹ and 544 cm⁻¹, γ-CoOOH at 579 cm⁻¹, and NiOOH at 477 cm⁻¹ and 553 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the electrochemical reconstruction progresses, the peaks of γ-NiOOH (465 cm⁻¹ and 544 cm⁻¹), γ-CoOOH (579 cm⁻¹) and NiOOH (477 cm⁻¹ and 553 cm⁻¹) begin to form.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows homogeneous Ni, Co, O distribution in Ni–Co oxyhydroxides with absence of P and S signals confirming successful conversion from Ni-Co-P@CoNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images reveal that... the lack of P and S signals and appearance of O signals after the electrochemical reconstruction process confirm that the Ni–Co–P@CoNi₂S₄ was successfully converted into Ni–Co oxyhydroxides.
